hints: Decide the first piece first. Which prefixes of s are allowed as the first piece, and what problem is left after you cut it?
Backtrack on a start index: try every end e where s[start..e] is a palindrome, add that piece and recurse from e+1. Optionally precompute a pal[i][j] table so each check is O(1).

1. Precompute pal[i][j]: true if s[i]==s[j] and (j-i < 2 or pal[i+1][j-1]).
  2. go(start): if start == n, save a copy of the pieces.
  3. For each end from start to n-1, if pal[start][end]:
  4. add s.substring(start, end+1), call go(end+1), remove it.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try all 2<sup>n-1</sup> ways to place cuts and check every piece with a two-pointer palindrome test.

approaches.name: Optimal: backtracking + palindrome table
approaches.idea: Only branch on palindromic pieces, with an O(n²) precomputed table for instant checks.

explain: For "noon": the first piece can be n or noon (no and noo are not palindromes). noon finishes a way immediately. After n, the rest oon can start with o (then o, n) or oo (then n). That gives 3 ways. A single letter is always a palindrome, so at least one way (all single letters) always exists.
recognize: 'Split a string into pieces where every piece satisfies a check, return all splits' → backtracking on the start index.
